workflow_runs.display_title: pm-258/t-1564: Run e2e files one at a time, give the footer walk and …

head_commit.message:
pm-258/t-1564: Run e2e files one at a time, give the footer walk and probe a throwaway database, and keep their checks apart from Kame

Since 76141f1 "E2E against next start" failed on frame floors (the
desk's leaves, the Ryugu sea) because node --test ran the browser files
side by side and they starved each other of frames. scripts/e2e.mjs now
passes --test-concurrency=1; a later flag still wins.
lib/e2e-runner.test.ts proves two files do not overlap, and that
--test-concurrency=2 makes them overlap.

scripts/e2e.mjs --serve-db <dir> holds its embedded Postgres, migrated,
until SIGTERM. walk-end.sh and probe-end.sh use it when no database
answers and Docker is absent, and stop only their own process and
work dir. e2e.mjs now owns SIGINT/SIGTERM: embedded-postgres's
async-exit-hook used to exit first and leave the work dir (and the
server group) behind.

The Kame companion (dd21add) broke two checks. The probe's eyes budget
counted Kame's scroll edge frame from a late setup scroll event: it now
waits for scrolling to go quiet, and a new rAF negative control
overlaps the two frames on purpose. ink-press's getByRole("status")
also matched Kame's live region: it is now scoped to the press.

The footer waterline checks were repaired concurrently by 3351f78
(pm-249/t-1568), so this commit does not touch them.

workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: pm-260/t-1578: Add offline split part release probe

head_commit.message:
pm-260/t-1578: Add offline split part release probe

lib/plan-release.ts evaluates decoded get_plan, explain_schedule,
get_timeline and list_runs payloads for a split part and reports
hold_released, queued_startable, execution_started, release_recorded and
dispatch_proven separately, with stable reasons. Identity mismatches and
unsupported shapes fail closed; absent progress is not a release; a
dispatch (even a failed attempt) never claims delivery.

scripts/probe-plan-release.mjs reads local snapshot files plus an
optional sha256/completeness manifest and exits 0/1/2 for
--require released|dispatched. The walkthrough documents collection
through the four MCP read tools and the QA negative controls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
pm-249/t-1568: Make CI checks green: teach the footer walk and probe the waterline, and wait for the sea's frames

The checks job on main stopped at "Footer walk" and "Footer Chromium probe" on every run, so production
(needs: checks) never deployed. 5cd6ee0 added the waterline (one aria-hidden wave and a /ryugu link) as the
footer's last child, and the two footer scripts still expected 3 SVGs and Back to top as the last Tab stop.
They now keep the 3 scene layers and also assert the waterline: last, one hidden wave, the /ryugu link,
nothing of the footer below it, and ryugu as the last Tab stop before focus leaves.

e2e/ryugu.test.ts judged the resumed sea by frames in a fixed 400 ms window, which on SwiftShader measured
frame rate (1 of 6 failed). It now waits, bounded, for the fish to swim again and then for the frames.

Every checks step ran locally in CI order and CI env against Postgres 17: all green (unit 2037, e2e 75,
motion 356, walk 65, probe 169).

head_commit.message:
pm-256/t-1559: Open Ryugu-jo below the waterline: urashima, Pocket and footer entries, WebGL caustics with a still fallback, fleeing ink fish

The palace is its own root layout at app/(ryugu)/ (/ryugu, static, noindex) with
its own sheet, so no site or cartridge styling reaches it. The server draws a
still sea (SVG-filter caustic, palace, seeded fish); the client adds WebGL water
and fish that flee pointer or touch only when WebGL works and motion is welcome,
asks for no context under reduced motion, and stops its loop while hidden.

Ways down: typing "urashima" (a capture listener in the site root layout that
takes the word's a's before the Pocket console sees them), a Dive chip on the
Pocket console, and a waterline link below the footer bar.

Tests: lib/urashima.test.ts, app/(ryugu)/_lib/{school,scene,isolation}.test.ts
(wired into npm test) and e2e/ryugu.test.ts.

head_commit.message:
pm-251/t-1546: Wait for the held key's press transition to land instead of sampling once at 200 ms

QA rep-5087 saw 3 of 8 letterpress runs fail the held-key check: under load the 70 ms press translate read 0px or mid-way at the fixed 200 ms sample. The probe now polls the translate for up to 2 s, and under reduced motion reads once after two animation frames. Locally 10 of 10 runs are green (5 under a concurrent typecheck), and removing the :active translate still fails both held-key checks.

head_commit.message:
pm-251/t-1543: Keep page 8's date inside the safe area in any serif, and wait for the Print button to come back

The green gate failed the 6 mm safe-area check on page 8's <time>. An inline box takes its font's ascent and
descent, and with Noto Serif that reached 1 px past the line, so past the safe edge. A Noto-only fontconfig
reproduces it locally (52/2). As an inline-block, the date is exactly one line tall whatever the font.

The probe's "ready again" check read isEnabled() as soon as the stubbed print() returned, before React committed
setBusy(false). It now waits up to 5 s for the button to be enabled. A build that never resets busy still fails
that check (53/1).

head_commit.message:
pm-249/t-1523: Hide a data-engineering text adventure in the Pocket Terminal; four secrets unlock a stamp and the walk is kept

`adventure` hands the prompt to lib/adventure.ts until quit. It is a pure state machine: eight rooms (The
Warehouse, The Lake, The Broken DAG, Staging Table, Cron Tavern and three more), four things to carry and four
secrets, with look/go/take/use/inventory/help/quit and n/s/e/w. The walk is saved to localStorage after every
line, inside try/catch, so private mode plays on in memory and says so once. The last secret adds "Keeper of the
Pipeline" to the terminal's stamps. Unit tests cover the full winning walk, resume and throwing storage; the e2e
reloads mid-walk and wins in real Chrome.
